AirScroll turns hand movement into scrolling and volume, so you can use your phone without touching it.
In the kitchen, with a recipe open and your hands covered in flour.
At work, with gloves, tools or dirty hands.

Get in frame, hold still, complete the circle, then try the two commands. At the end you get a report of what was measured, and you can redo just the weak part instead of starting over. Watch the animation: that is exactly the movement.
Numbers are in hundredths of the frame — what matters is comparing them with each other, not their absolute value.
Hand up scrolls the page up instead of down.
Battery uses a smaller image and the CPU only. Responsive raises the frame rate on capable phones.
Red off, amber waiting, green active.
Turn off the ones you do not want armed. You can add any other app by its package name.
Camera permission is missing: the engine cannot see your hand.

AirScroll needs this service to scroll on your behalf inside other apps. It does not read the content of your screen: it only sees which app is in the foreground, and sends the swipe gestures that your hand movement produces.
Turns hand movement into scrolling, offline.
V with two fingers — say it
Hold up two fingers for a moment: the microphone opens for six seconds.
Only if you switched voice commands on in the settings. The microphone closes on its own, and Android shows its own indicator at the top while it is open.
Open source · Everything runs offline on your phone
Since Android 13, apps installed outside an app store cannot turn on the accessibility service until you unlock it once. If the switch looks greyed out, or you see \"Restricted setting\", do this:
Open the app info with the button below.
Tap the three dots in the top right corner.
Tap \"Allow restricted settings\", then come back here.

Play Protect may also call AirScroll harmful. It flags any sideloaded app that asks for the camera together with the accessibility service — the combination stalkerware uses. AirScroll has no internet permission at all and the code is public, so you can check for yourself. Choose \"Install anyway\" to continue.
It is what sees your hand. The images stay inside this app for the time of one frame: nothing is saved, nothing is sent.
It is the only way an app can scroll inside another app. AirScroll asks for the smallest version of it: it can send gestures, it cannot read your screen.
Three details that make it work well
None of them is mandatory, but without them something will feel broken.
Instead of asking you to guess numbers, AirScroll measures your real hand: how far you hold it, how much it shakes, how wide your comfortable movement is.
Fake content that really scrolls with your hand, right inside the app. No accessibility service needed, so you can check that the gestures work before anything else.
Try the gestures without leaving the app
Same engine as the real thing, on fake content. The best place to tune sensitivity and dead zone.
Move these while you scroll: the effect is immediate, and what you set here is what the real thing will do.
Scroll your hand up and down. The text follows you, exactly as if a finger were resting on the screen and dragging it.
There are no jumps and no commands. What the camera sees is a position, and that position becomes a speed: the further your hand goes from the resting point, the faster the page moves.
Around the resting point there is a dead zone, shaped on the tremor measured during calibration. Inside it nothing happens, which is why holding still keeps the page still.
Only one axis moves at a time. Once the vertical takes over, sideways drift is ignored until you come back to the middle — otherwise scrolling would keep changing the volume by accident.
If your hand slowly drifts while you read, the resting point drifts with it. It is a small thing that avoids the most annoying failure: a page that scrolls on its own because your arm got tired.
Close your fist for about two seconds to stop. Out there, in a real app, leaving the app stops it too, and the camera closes with it.
And here is something to scroll past
Yellow · waiting for a thumbs up
Hand at 20-30 cm. Wide movements, gentler response.
Hand at 40-60 cm. The balanced choice.
Hand beyond 70 cm. Small movements, stronger response.
Follows the hand size seen by the camera, using your calibration.
Frames are being sent but the model is not answering. This is a bug, not your hand: please report it with this screen.
Records how your hand looks to the model, so the thresholds can be tuned on real numbers instead of guesses.
Five short takes. Only numbers are saved — the 21 hand points and the recognised gesture. No image is ever written to the file, and nothing leaves your phone unless you choose to share it.
The file is on your phone. Open it if you want to see exactly what it contains: it is plain text.
Hold a thumbs up steady, the way you would to start scrolling.
Close your fist and hold it, the way you would to stop.
Open hand, still. This teaches the app what should NOT start anything.
Move your hand up and down as if scrolling, at your natural pace.
Lower your hand or move it out of frame. This shows what the camera sees when you are not asking for anything.
AirScroll speaks Italian, English, Spanish, German and Chinese. \"System\" follows your phone.
Hand recognition could not start: the recognition model is not inside this build. The camera works, but no gesture will ever be detected.
Hand recognition could not start: the recognition model is packed compressed and cannot be opened. This is a packaging bug, not a problem with your phone.

Hand recognition could not start: the recognition library is not compatible with this phone, which uses %1$d KB memory pages. It is a known incompatibility and it is fixed by updating the library, not by changing anything on your side.
Hand recognition could not start: the recognition library could not be loaded on this phone.
Hand recognition could not start. The technical details are below: please send them, they say exactly what went wrong.

Hold your hand still in front of the camera, at the distance you would normally use. Two and a half seconds: this measures how much your hand trembles and how big it looks, and marks your resting point.
Move your hand outwards in every direction, as if drawing a circle in the air. Each segment lights up when you reach it. Move as far as is comfortable — not as far as you possibly can.
This is far enough for me
Open hand, palm towards the screen, 20 to 40 cm away — the distance you will actually use.
Move your whole forearm, not just your fingers: recognition follows the middle of your palm.
One slow lap, about five seconds. Moving fast makes the camera lose your hand.
Go as far as is comfortable, not as far as you can strain. This should look like the way you will really use it.
Stay inside the frame. If the dot turns red, the camera has lost you: come back towards the middle.
Every gesture, moving. The details are the ones that are not obvious the first time.

Hold it for about half a second, not just a flash. A brief dip — your hand rotates, a finger covers the thumb — does not reset the count: it picks up again. But clearly making a different gesture does reset it, because that means you changed your mind.

Speed is progressive: a small movement scrolls slowly, a wide one scrolls fast. Small tremors do nothing at all — the neutral zone measured during calibration absorbs them. And each direction only asks for what your hand can actually reach.

One axis at a time: while you are scrolling you cannot change the volume by accident, and the other axis has to win by a clear margin to take over. The horizontal axis can also be switched off entirely in Settings.
Two seconds, so you do not stop by accident. Adjustable in Settings → Timings. Opening your hand before the two seconds are up cancels the stop.

The amber window also closes on its own after about six seconds without a thumbs up, and the camera goes off. To reopen it without leaving the app, tap “Look for the hand” on the AirScroll notification.
The page goes where you put your hand and stays there, as if you were dragging it. Push further and it keeps scrolling; flick your hand back and it carries on and slows down.
Your hand sets the speed: the further from centre, the faster it scrolls, and it keeps going until you come back. This is how it worked up to version 0.4.5.
The manual and the privacy notice travel inside the app: AirScroll cannot reach the network, and a document explaining exactly that would be a contradiction if you needed a connection to read it.
The document could not be opened. There may be no PDF reader installed.
Until now every statement about battery use in this project was reasoning, never measured. Three phases of twenty seconds each turn it into a number.

Absolute consumption would say almost nothing: the screen alone weighs more than everything else together. What counts is the comparison between a phone doing nothing and the same phone running AirScroll, measured seconds apart.
Keep the screen on and the brightness unchanged for all three phases, and do not touch anything. About a minute in total.
AirScroll is doing nothing. This is the yardstick: it is what your phone costs just by being on.
The camera is open at the waiting rate, with no recognition. This is the cost of the sensor alone.
Camera and recognition at full rate, as when you are actually controlling something. Hold your hand in front of it if you like: it changes nothing for the measurement.
AirScroll costs about %1$d mA while waiting and %2$d mA while active, on top of the phone.
At this rate, continuous use would drain a full battery in roughly %1$.1f hours. It is an order of magnitude, not a promise.

The current sensor is not equally accurate on every phone, and the screen dominates the total. Trust the difference between the rows, not the absolute values, and compare measurements taken on the same phone.
These numbers do not add up: the phone may not report current reliably, or something else was running. Try again with nothing else open.
This phone does not report the current being drawn, so the meter cannot work here. It is a limit of the device, not of the app.
The phone is charging: current is flowing in, not out, and the measurement would be meaningless. Unplug it first.

Two savings under one switch: the camera is asked to capture more slowly instead of running flat out and throwing frames away, and while waiting, frames that have not changed are not analysed at all. The second one switches itself off the moment a hand appears. Turn the whole thing off to see, with the battery meter, how much it is actually worth.
No preset: your own sliders decide.
Hands busy, phone on the counter. Wider neutral zone and calmer scrolling, because floury hands move badly and you are following a recipe, not a feed.

Phone outside on a shelf, further away. Everything more forgiving, and a much longer amber window: under running water nobody reacts in six seconds. Expect steam and distance to make recognition harder.
Phone on a shelf, close, one hand busy. Like the kitchen but nearer and calmer: here you are usually reading.

Phone in its mount. The strictest preset, for a different reason from the others: here a false positive is not an inconvenience. Very wide neutral zone, a longer thumbs up to activate, slow scrolling. Volume stays, but needs a wide, deliberate movement. Do not read while driving.
Warns you when AirScroll stops working, and says how to fix it.
AirScroll is off after the restart
The phone was restarted and AirScroll did not come back on its own — on purpose: an app that restarts itself and opens the camera is exactly what nobody wants. Open the app and switch it back on.
Your phone closed the service to save battery, so your hand no longer controls anything. Turn it back on from the app. To stop it happening again, remove AirScroll from battery optimisation.
AirScroll still sees your hand but can no longer touch the screen. Android sometimes turns this off by itself after a system update. Switch it back on under Settings → Accessibility → AirScroll.
Without the camera there is nothing to recognise. Grant it under Settings → Apps → AirScroll → Permissions.
MediaPipe failed to start on this phone. Open AirScroll: the screen shows the full technical report, with a button to copy it.
Another app is using the camera
AirScroll is waiting for it to be free: close the video call or the app holding it and everything resumes on its own. There is nothing to change in the settings.
The status dot is on in the settings but permission to draw over other apps is missing. Everything else works — you just cannot see which state you are in.
Your phone can close AirScroll at any time
It has already happened at least once. While AirScroll is subject to battery optimisation, the system can stop it whenever it likes, without warning.
Before measuring anything, AirScroll checks that it can measure: hand in frame, at the right distance, near the middle. Hold it steady for a moment and it moves on by itself.
Show your open hand to the camera
Come closer — your hand is too far away
Move back a little — your hand is too close
Move towards the middle of the frame

Nothing is measured here. It checks that the two gestures that start and stop everything are recognised on your hand — the one check that was missing, and without it you would only find out during real use.
Now a closed fist, and hold it
This gesture is not being recognised. It may be the light, the angle, or this particular hand. You can move on: the report will say it was not recognised, instead of pretending otherwise.
Usable calibration, with a weak spot
One part is too weak to keep

One direction reaches much further than its opposite. That is normal — arms are built that way — and it is exactly why one direction will feel different from the other. AirScroll now knows, and compensates.

No wake word, and no listening in the background. The microphone opens only after you hold up a V with two fingers, stays open for six seconds, and closes on its own. Recognition happens on the phone: AirScroll has no internet permission, so the audio could not leave even if it wanted to.
Needs the microphone permission. Everything else keeps working without it.

This phone has no on-device speech recognition (it needs Android 12 or newer, with the system speech model installed). Voice stays off: the only alternative would be sending your audio to a server, and that is not an alternative.
Commands are spoken in Italian. This list is everything AirScroll understands: anything else does nothing.
Calibration and settings in one readable text file. Export it before changing phone — or before an update that forces you to reinstall.
That file is not an AirScroll profile: nothing was changed
